    Split the website packs by ownership: public-website, github-pages, cloudflare-site (#2101)
    
    * Split the GitHub Pages half of static-website into a github-pages pack
    
    static-website conflated two things: what is true of a static site (a version
    scheme, an explicit publish set, a config file, a PR gate) and what is true of
    one served from GitHub Pages (release on push, the Release it cuts, the Pages
    deploy, the subpath it is served from). A repo hosting its site anywhere else
    could take only half the pack, and the half it left behind was where three of
    the four checks lived.
    
    The serving half is now its own pack. github-pages holds the orchestrator and
    the three reusable workflows (renamed github-pages-*), the gp/pages-workflows
    check, the subpath rule, the releasing-to-github-pages skill, its own standing
    vendoring record, and the one-time repository settings as adoptionHandover.
    It requires static-website, whose composite actions its workflows still run.
    
    static-website keeps the version scheme, site.config, the publish set, the
    three actions and the PR gate. Its checks can no longer gate on an orchestrator
    that has left the pack, so relevance moves to adoptedStandard: the site config
    OR the vendored CI gate, either sufficient — two independent signals, because
    the missing config is itself the thing sw/site-config exists to report. The
    presence half of the departed sw/release-workflows becomes sw/vendored-pipeline
    over the files the pack still owns.
    
    The pack has no adopters since EdFringeNow removed it, so nothing is migrated
    and no legacy spelling is carried. Open question 1 of docs/website-release-flows
    is answered against D1 and recorded there.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Put sw/version-scheme on the same relevance gate as its three siblings
    
    The README claimed relevance for all four checks was adoptedStandard, but
    version-scheme still opened on its own read of site.config — the same
    inconsistency this split exists to remove, reintroduced one file down.
    
    No behaviour changes: a missing config already short-circuited the rule, and
    still does on the line below the gate, which now says out loud that
    sw/site-config owns that case. What changes is that the four rules read alike
    and the README's claim about them is true.
    
    CONFIG_PATH now comes from vendored-pipeline, its one definition, rather than
    through a re-export site-config.mjs was only carrying for other modules.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Leave the website-release-flows design doc alone
    
    A DESIGN.md carries the end state and its rationale — never progress, a
    superseded-decision narrative or an owner attribution, which is what the
    state note I added was made of. The record that the split answers its open
    question 1 against D1 belongs in the pull request, where it already is.

    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Name the Pages skill for what it does, and cut it to the actions
    
    It does not perform a release — it wires, changes and debugs the vendored
    pipeline that does, so it is github-pages-pipeline now and its description
    says which moments want it.
    
    Halved: the stage-by-stage narrative of the publish reusable is that file's
    own header comment, and what the pack does and does not own is the README's.
    What is left is the three steps that wire a repo, a table of the four things
    anyone actually drives it to do, and the two facts that surprise people — the
    pipeline writes no version of its own, and a GITHUB_TOKEN push fires no
    workflow.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Cut both packs' rules to the ration, evidence into references.md
    
    Every rule ran 150-200 words where the format asks for one sentence near 40,
    and several opened on a state of the world ("A published file is a file the
    publish set names") rather than on the act that brings a reader to them.
    
    Each is now keyed to what the reader is doing — adding a file the site serves,
    changing the publish set, deciding a cache lifetime — and carries only the
    consequence needed to apply it under pressure. Nothing is weakened and nothing
    is strengthened: the rationale moves to each pack's new references.md, which
    no session loads and which exists so a later pass can reaffirm or retire a
    rule from its recorded reason. The evidence goes with it, the 0-bytes-of-3.1MB
    timezone rewrite and the join check that passed at 6% included.
    
    One rule's subject pointed back at its neighbour with a "that", so it read as
    a clause rather than a situation; it stands alone now.
    
    Five of static-website's rules are rewritten in place and one is genuinely
    retired — the subpath rule, which moved to github-pages with the split. That
    is what rules-append-only reports on this change.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Publish the workflow-run and Pages reads a release worker needs
    
    A worker that dispatches a workflow gets a 204 and no run id, so it
    finds its run as the workflow's newest dispatch and polls it; and a
    Pages release probes the site at the URL the Pages API names. Three
    operations on the port, published through the public seam, with the
    fake port taught the same names.
    
    Refs #2101
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Rename static-website to public-website and keep only what is true of a website
    
    The pack stops carrying anything about how a site is built, served or
    released: the site config, the composite actions, the CI gate and their
    checks leave for the hosting packs. What stays is what is true of a
    public website whatever serves it — the version and the stamp its pages
    show, and the client-side caching rules.
    
    The version scheme is cloudflare-site's, brought in unchanged (years
    since 2025, a monotonic build, package.json as the one record), and
    exposed through the pack's public/ seam so a hosting pack's release can

    same function over git's file list. Every tracked page carrying the

    The pack names no host and reads no host's file. The rename map carries
    the old spelling and a record converges declarations onto the new one.
    
    Refs #2101
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Rebuild github-pages as a nightly release task over one deploy workflow
    
    A Pages deploy is made of marketplace actions only a workflow job can

    moved past the last release, it advances the version through

156:[16:41:11] USER: Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/writing-tests # Testing practices A consuming repo's own test *mechanics* — runner, layout, which suites exist — are its own docs'; CI-trigger rules and the `GITHUB_TOKEN` workflow-recursion gotcha are [git-github-advanced](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md)'s. - See a test fail before you trust it: write it red before the fix (green after), or break what it guards and watch it go red. A test that has never failed proves nothing. For a **refusal/negative** test — one asserting a guard yields *nothing* — the write-it-red-first branch is unavailable: the pre-change code also yielded nothing, so the test passes from birth and proves nothing. See-it-fail there **must** be the second method — mutate the new guard (weaken it), watch the test bite, then restore it. Restore with `git checkout -- <file>` (or `git stash`) taken at the moment of mutating — never a `.bak` copy saved earlier, which predates whatever else you edited in between and silently discards that intervening work. If the mutation was **staged** (to make a check that scans `git diff --cached` fire), a bare `git checkout -- <file>` restores from the index — which now holds the mutation — so the "restore" is a no-op; use `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` (or `git reset` first). - A mechanism meant to survive a retry, re-queue, or hand-off needs a test that calls it twice, not once. A suite of single-call tests stays green while the multi-call case corrupts state — the double-call is what a real retry, requeue, or hand-off actually does. When the mechanism arbitrates by identity (a claim, a lock), the second call must come from a **different actor**: a single actor retrying its own stale claim can't expose an identity-masked race, since it still recognizes its own claim as valid. - A simulator of a stateful mechanism must advance state only where the real engine's code actually leaves a mark — never wherever the rule's stated description says a transition happens. A sim that fires on every event matching the rule's *intent* is correct by construction against that rule and blind to exactly the silent paths where the real implementation and the rule have quietly diverged — which is where a genuine bug usually lives. Read the real engine's code for what it *writes*, and model that. - Before trusting a new transform/normalizer, run it over the *real existing corpus* it will process, not just hand-picked test inputs — the live data exposes edge cases your examples won't. # Running the suite

- **The whole suite is one command** — `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`. There is no test
  script; `ci.yml`'s array is not authoritative. A bash glob without `globstar` is the dangerous
  substitute — it reached 37 of 65 files and reported nothing wrong — while `node --test <dir>`
  fails outright, so only the glob leaves you believing a green run. (4)
- **Read a run's output from a file** — redirect one run and grep that file for the slice you need;
  never re-run the ~55s suite to re-slice unchanged output. (1)
- **`git add` a new test file before certifying a run green** — `git ls-files` excludes an unstaged
  file, so the run never executed it; the `untracked-test-file` finding at Stop says which. (2)
- **Iterating on a sweep across many files** — run only the test files the edit touches, plus
  `check_the_work`; spend the whole suite and `check_the_world` once, at the end. Both are
  whole-tree aggregates whose verdict cannot turn on one file. (3)
- **Editing a `RULES.md` or `README.md` under `packs/`** — the file that holds a pack's rule index
  in step with its prose sits outside the pack, and neither conformance sweep runs it, so add
  `node --test engine-tests/rule-index.test.mjs` to the files the edit touches. (5)

# Writing a check that scans the repo

- **Choosing the file set** — take it from `git ls-files` rather than a filesystem walk with
  paths to skip, and remember a brand-new file is untracked until you add it, so a green run
  isn't coverage of it.

- **Scanning for a forbidden token** — strip comments first so it matches code, not prose —
  string-aware, since a `//` inside a URL is not a comment. Reuse `stripComments` from
  [`engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs`](../../../../engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs);
  if the scan can't import it, inline the same pass and point a comment back at that source.
  Strip in **both** directions — a comment that documents or warns about the banned pattern is
  exactly where a naive check trips over its own reasoning, so a commented-out instance must not
  count as present either.

- **Proving the check silent** — run it against the repo's own **real** sources, not only a
  synthetic clean fixture — a fixture spelling the same gap the check has just keeps proving the
  matching, and only a real-tree run can disagree with you.

members failing to converge looked like one member failing to converge, fourth
cell in, in ordinary ink. The state of the mounts is what the band is read for
first, so it is now the first cell, and past sqrt(members) stale it is the
fleet that has stopped updating rather than a few stragglers — the figure goes
red and bold and its line names the count, since at that point no single member
is the thing to go and look at.

engine, never converged, or carrying no stamp at all.

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot-authored
  # PR flow (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.
  workflow_dispatch:
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:

# Committing

- **One concern per commit.** If two changes could each stand alone, split them; a message that
  wants numbered items is the split talking.
- **Reference the issue, when the change has one** — `Refs #n`, or `Fixes #n` / `Closes #n` where

  else was in progress.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Guard a session transcript located by newest mtime rather than by id

From the 2026-09-18 window. #2111's session had to diagnose a first reply
that stopped after its announcements, and the transcript holding it was in
another container — an EdFringeNow session — so the diagnostic went over as
a script for that session to run. It picked its transcript as the newest
.jsonl under every directory in ~/.claude/projects, which is always the
transcript of the session running the script, so it diagnosed itself; the
receiving session said so and reproduced the case by hand instead.

The same mistake in its other spelling cost 2026-07-19's #366: capture-log
derived the transcript directory from the git-root path slug, which a
remote session's launch cwd does not match, and the fix there was the one
this guard names — resolve <sessionId>.jsonl through findTranscript, which
searches every project directory for the file the id names.

transcript-found-by-mtime fires at PreToolUse on a Bash or Write call whose
payload carries mtime, projects and .jsonl together, and stays silent when
it names findTranscript or capture-log.mjs. Red-first against the real
script's shape in both spellings; silent against the four reads that carry
one token alone.

input.title: SURFACE.GENERATED.md is stale since #2101, so pack-surface.test.mjs fails under CI on every branch
input.body:
`packs/claudinite-tasks/public/SURFACE.GENERATED.md` no longer matches what
`packs/claudinite-canon-curation/test/pack-surface.test.mjs` renders from the tree, so the
assertion that only runs under CI is red on current `main` (`016728d`) and on every branch cut
from it.

Reproduced on a clean checkout of `main`:

```
CI=1 node --test packs/claudinite-canon-curation/test/pack-surface.test.mjs
```

fails with `SURFACE.GENERATED.md is stale`. Running it without `CI` rewrites the file; the diff is
two rows, both the `github-pages` pack #2101 (`9750ab1`) added as a consumer:

- `delivery.mjs` — consumers gain `github-pages`
- `github.mjs` — `9` named / `9` taken (was `6` / `6`), consumers gain `github-pages`

Fix: run the test locally so it regenerates the file, and commit the result.

Nothing reported it at merge time: a merge to `main` here is pushed with the app token, which fires
no workflow, so `ci.yml`'s push trigger has produced no run on `main` since 2026-09-07 and the PR
run is the only one left.

Found while running the growth-extract task, whose own PR cannot carry the fix — its automerge
policy is `under:.claudinite/local` and the `growth-write-scope` check reds any path outside the
repo's local packs.

_Filed by the Claudinite task `claudinite-growth/growth-extract`, running as work item missingbulb/Claudinite#2119 — no person asked for this issue._

input.title: No canon rule says a pack file may not name another pack — the owner has corrected it twice, two months apart
input.body:
Two owner corrections in the conversation record say the same thing, and nothing on the shelf
carries it.

- 2026-07-19, capture `2026-07-19T2127Z--issue-364`: *"I can't understand why you insist on
  referring to canon-curation in packs/grow_with_claudinite. Its just comments. Just don't mention
  the things outside the pack. It's really so simple."*
- 2026-09-17, capture `2026-09-18T0559Z--pr-2101`, on
  `packs/claudinite-tasks/migrations/2026-08-31-executor-vars-bag/migration.mjs:13`: *"Stop
  refering to other packs from packs. All those renames in the migration.mjs records are
  redundant. Eliminate them."* — landed as #2101's commit *"Drop the comments that cited another
  pack's record as an example"*.

What exists today does not cover it:

- `packs/basics` `config.barriers` guards `engine → packs/*` and `packs/* → docs`, not
  `packs/* → packs/*` for a plain mention. The `siblings: 'packs'` + `scope: 'imports'` edge the
  2026-07 session built covered imports only, and is not in the settings file now.
- `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/RULES.md` has *"A canon pack's prose naming another pack by
  literal path — check the name resolves inside every consumer's vendored tree"*, which sanctions
  the mention it asks you to verify.
- `packs/claudinite-growth/RULES.md`'s RULES-2 says it, but only for that one pack.

Both corrections were about a **comment**, which is the shape neither the barrier nor the prose
catches: an illustrative "the same shape as `<other pack>`" that the sentence stands without.

Proposed: a `config.barriers` edge `{ siblings: 'packs', to: 'packs/*' }` over all reference kinds
with the exemptions the tree actually needs, and canon-curation's rule rewritten from "check it
resolves" to "don't name it". Sizing the exemption list against the current tree is the first step
— that is what decides whether this is one change or a migration.

The growth-extract run that found this cannot land it: the lesson is
`claudinite-canon-curation`'s territory, which its local pack's `ruleRoutingGuidance` excludes and
its write scope forbids.

_Filed by the Claudinite task `claudinite-growth/growth-extract`, running as work item missingbulb/Claudinite#2119 — no person asked for this issue._

input.title: Claudinite growth: extract lessons
input.head: claudinite/claudinite-growth/growth-extract/2026-09-18-qka1sp
input.body:
One check into the repo's own local pack, from the 2026-09-18 window
(`016728d`, `9750ab1`, `4e16770`, `6d5dcbc`, `b614777`; captures
`2026-09-17T1041Z`–`2026-09-18T0604Z`, plus the hindsight window at the branch's
oldest end, `2026-07-19T1509Z`–`2026-07-20T1358Z`).

### What landed

`transcript-found-by-mtime` — an action guard on a Bash or Write call whose payload carries
`mtime`, `projects` and `.jsonl` together, silent when it names `findTranscript` or
`capture-log.mjs`. `blocking`, `since: 2026-09-18`.

The evidence is two firings of one mistake, two months apart:

- **2026-09-17, #2111.** The owner asked why a session had replied only `Comment class:
  process-change` and stopped. The transcript holding it belonged to an EdFringeNow session in
  another container, so the diagnostic went across as a script for that session to run. It chose
  its transcript as the newest `.jsonl` across every directory under `~/.claude/projects` — which
  is always the transcript of the session running the script. The receiving session reported back
  *"Only one transcript exists on this box and it is this session's own file, so the script
  diagnosed itself"*, listed the script's defects, and reproduced the case by hand anyway. One
  hand-off round spent on a selector that could not have worked.
- **2026-07-19, #366.** `capture-log.mjs` derived the transcript directory from the git-root path
  slug, which a remote session's launch cwd does not match, and every EdFringeNow capture silently
  found nothing. The fix then is the one the guard's `fix` names now:
  `findTranscript({ root, sessionId })` searches every project directory for `<sessionId>.jsonl`,
  which is exact wherever the session ran.

Red-first: the test asserts the real script's shape fires under both spellings it arrives by (a
heredoc and a `Write`), and stays silent on four ordinary reads that carry one of the three tokens
alone — a `findTranscript` import, an `ls` of the projects directory, `ls -lt --time=mtime`, and a
`git show` of a capture file. Seen failing before the declaration existed, green after.

### What did not land, and why

- **A pack file naming another pack.** The window's strongest owner correction — *"Stop refering to
  other packs from packs"* (#2101), matching the same correction on 2026-07-19 — is
  `claudinite-canon-curation`'s territory, which this local pack's `ruleRoutingGuidance` excludes
  and this task's write scope forbids. Filed as #2126 with both citations and a proposed barrier
  edge.
- **#2099's two-root bug** (`consumerBucket` matching the pack prefix literally, so the pack reached
  through `.claudinite/shared/` read as an external consumer) is already RULES-26.
- **The cross-session prompt disclaimer** the owner asked for on 2026-07-19 appears nowhere in the
  corpus and is still being honoured — it lives in the personal preference file, which never
  becomes a pack rule.
- **No prose.** The one keeper was expressible as a check, so the `RULES.md` ration went unspent and
  the upgrade pass over this run's own additions had nothing to convert.

### Verification

Suite 3725/3729; the four failures are pre-existing and unrelated — two shallow-clone guards that
fail loudly by design here, and the two `local-rules` rehearsals, both reproduced with this change
stashed. `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` clean, with the advisory set byte-identical to
the pre-change run.

Note for whoever reviews this PR's CI: `pack-surface.test.mjs` is red on `main` itself since #2101
left `SURFACE.GENERATED.md` stale, so it will be red here too. Filed as #2125 — this PR cannot
carry the fix, which is outside `under:.claudinite/local`.

Refs #2119

# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request

How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.

## The branch and the pull request were chosen for you

**Push to the `Target-branch:` your item carries, and onto the `Target-pr:` where it
carries one.** The executor resolved both from the task's `expected_outcome` before
your session started: `fresh_pr` gave you a new branch and left the task's earlier pull
requests alone; `amend_existing_or_create_new_pr` gave you the branch of the task's
newest open pull request when it had no conflicts, and a fresh one otherwise;
`supersede_existing_pr` gave you a fresh branch and listed the earlier ones under
`Supersedes:`. Where there is a `Target-pr:`, push onto it and open nothing — the pull
request already exists and your push updates it. Where there is none, open your pull
request on that branch. Never mint a branch name, never search for an open pull
request to reuse, and never close an earlier run's pull request yourself: the converge
(`src/session/converge-item.mjs`, handed `--pr`) closes what `Supersedes:` names once yours
exists, and a run that delivered nothing leaves them where they were.

## Say which task wrote it

**Every commit you push on a task's behalf carries `Claudinite-Task: <pack>/<task>` on
its own line** — the pack and task id from the work item's first line. When you merge,
put the same line in the squash commit's message too: the merge commit is what lands on
the default branch, and it is the one the signal collectors read.

That trailer is how the scheduler tells the project moving from the machinery running. A
task's own delivery must never count as the repo activity that wakes the next task, and
a title is not a reliable way to say so — every new task's title is a new leak. Yours
says it in the commit.

## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest

Your task's declared `automerge` is a **ceiling, not a plan** (the legacy
`expected_outcome: 'open-pr'` reads as `fresh_pr` with `nothing`, `'merged-pr'` as
`fresh_pr` with `anything`; `none` and `pr` read as `no_code_changes` and `fresh_pr`).
On a request item the authorization is the item's **`Merge:` field** instead,
read within that ceiling: absent means `nothing`, `if-narrow` means the
`narrow-diff` composite, and any other value is the policy expression itself.
Whichever source it came from:

- **`nothing`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
  applies to you.
- **`anything`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.
- **a policy list** (e.g. `['comment-only-changes', 'readme-changes']`, a folder
  scope such as `['under:product-wiki']`, or an intersection of the two,
  `['under:product-wiki && doc-changes']`) — the task may
  land its PR only when the diff sits inside the policy, and the policy engine decides
  that, never your reading of the diff. Before step 2, run it from the repository root —
  `src/session/merge-policy-run.mjs` in the claudinite-tasks pack (probe
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/src/session/merge-policy-run.mjs`, falling back to
  `packs/claudinite-tasks/src/session/merge-policy-run.mjs` in the canon):

  ```
  node <that file> --base <the PR's base branch> --policy '<the terms, ;-joined>'
  ```

  `AUTOMERGE: no` — leave the PR open for review, quote the verdict line in your wrap-up,
  and stop; a diff wider than its policy waiting for a person is a correct outcome, and
  you never re-shape a change to fit the classifier. `AUTOMERGE: yes` — amend your
  branch's final commit to carry the arming trailer on its own line,
  `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy: <the same expression>`, push, and continue below (the
  `automerge-policy-scope` check re-measures the diff against the trailer, so a
  mis-measured arm goes red instead of merging).

## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference

`.claudinite-settings.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:

- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading an
  authorized landing to review is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
  materializing it is the update converge's job, not yours.
- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the work item.

## 2. Arm auto-merge

Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
it once this repo's required checks pass.

## 3. When the arm is rejected

- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
  PR's **head sha**:
  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the ceiling — the trail
    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
    unseen check does not survive anything.

## Never

Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
are always legal outcomes.

input.body:
Provenance: the `transcript-found-by-mtime` check in #2127 draws its second occurrence from this issue's captured session (`2026-07-19T2059Z--issue-366`, session `1952b8c3`).

The report here was that `capture-log.mjs` found no transcript in an EdFringeNow session and pushed nothing. The cause was the same class of mistake the new guard is about: the transcript was located by a proxy rather than by the session it belongs to — the project directory derived from the git-root path slug, which a remote session's launch cwd does not match. The fix landed in this issue is what the guard now names as the remedy: `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is the transcript's filename stem, so `findTranscript({ root, sessionId })` searches every project directory for `<sessionId>.jsonl` and is exact wherever the session ran.

The other proxy — newest mtime — reappeared on 2026-09-17 in a hand-written diagnostic, which is what put the two firings two months apart over the bar. No change is asked for here; this comment is the trail from the rule back to its first evidence.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: mcp__github__get_job_logs
entries.description:
Get logs for GitHub Actions workflow jobs.
Use this tool to retrieve logs for a specific job or all failed jobs in a workflow run.
For single job logs, provide job_id. For all failed jobs in a run, provide run_id with failed_only=true.

failed_only.description: When true, gets logs for all failed jobs in the workflow run specified by run_id. Requires run_id to be provided.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow job. Required when getting logs for a single job.

return_content.description: Returns actual log content instead of URLs

run_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run. Required when failed_only is true to get logs for all failed jobs in the run.

tail_lines.description: Number of lines to return from the end of the log

input.title: The local-rules rehearsal fixture points $schema at a pack its member never declares, so both its modes have been red since #2058
input.body:
`vendoring/rehearsal/rehearsal.test.mjs` fails on current `main` (`016728d`) in both modes of the
`local-rules` fixture, and has since #2058 (`e739e6e`, 2026-09-15) added `schema-conformance` and
the fixture's `$schema` pointer in the same change:

```
FAIL  local-rules [fresh]
  check-the-world:
    [BLOCKING] schema-conformance  .claudinite/local/packs/fixture-local/tasks/fixture-task/task.json:2
      points at .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/task.schema.json as its schema, which is not in the tree
    1 blocking, 0 advisory (world scope: all vs main).
```

`FIXTURE_TASK` (`vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs:338`) declares

```
"$schema": "../../../../../shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/task.schema.json"
```

while the fixture member declares `['basics', 'local/fixture-local']`. `claudinite-tasks` is not
among them, so nothing vendors that schema into the fixture's mount and the pointer resolves to a
path the tree does not hold. The two `local-rules` subtests plus their parent suite are the whole
of `# fail 3` on a CI run of a branch that changed nothing outside `.claudinite/local/packs/`
(run 35334042712), so every PR inherits it.

Either the fixture declares `claudinite-tasks` so the schema is vendored, or its task drops the
`$schema` field — whichever matches what a member in the `#555` shape really looks like.

Found while running the growth-extract task; its PR's automerge policy is
`under:.claudinite/local`, which cannot carry a fix under `vendoring/`.

_Filed by the Claudinite task `claudinite-growth/growth-extract`, running as work item missingbulb/Claudinite#2119 — no person asked for this issue._

input.body:
One check into the repo's own local pack, from the 2026-09-18 window
(`016728d`, `9750ab1`, `4e16770`, `6d5dcbc`, `b614777`; captures
`2026-09-17T1041Z`–`2026-09-18T0604Z`, plus the hindsight window at the branch's
oldest end, `2026-07-19T1509Z`–`2026-07-20T1358Z`).

### What landed

`transcript-found-by-mtime` — an action guard on a Bash or Write call whose payload carries
`mtime`, `projects` and `.jsonl` together, silent when it names `findTranscript` or
`capture-log.mjs`. `blocking`, `since: 2026-09-18`.

The evidence is two firings of one mistake, two months apart:

- **2026-09-17, #2111.** The owner asked why a session had replied only `Comment class:
  process-change` and stopped. The transcript holding it belonged to an EdFringeNow session in
  another container, so the diagnostic went across as a script for that session to run. It chose
  its transcript as the newest `.jsonl` across every directory under `~/.claude/projects` — which
  is always the transcript of the session running the script. The receiving session reported back
  *"Only one transcript exists on this box and it is this session's own file, so the script
  diagnosed itself"*, listed the script's defects, and reproduced the case by hand anyway. One
  hand-off round spent on a selector that could not have worked.
- **2026-07-19, #366.** `capture-log.mjs` derived the transcript directory from the git-root path
  slug, which a remote session's launch cwd does not match, and every EdFringeNow capture silently
  found nothing. The fix then is the one the guard's `fix` names now:
  `findTranscript({ root, sessionId })` searches every project directory for `<sessionId>.jsonl`,
  which is exact wherever the session ran.

Red-first: the test asserts the real script's shape fires under both spellings it arrives by (a
heredoc and a `Write`), and stays silent on four ordinary reads that carry one of the three tokens
alone — a `findTranscript` import, an `ls` of the projects directory, `ls -lt --time=mtime`, and a
`git show` of a capture file. Seen failing before the declaration existed, green after.

### What did not land, and why

- **A pack file naming another pack.** The window's strongest owner correction — *"Stop refering to
  other packs from packs"* (#2101), matching the same correction on 2026-07-19 — is
  `claudinite-canon-curation`'s territory, which this local pack's `ruleRoutingGuidance` excludes
  and this task's write scope forbids. Filed as #2126 with both citations and a proposed barrier
  edge.
- **#2099's two-root bug** (`consumerBucket` matching the pack prefix literally, so the pack reached
  through `.claudinite/shared/` read as an external consumer) is already RULES-26.
- **The cross-session prompt disclaimer** the owner asked for on 2026-07-19 appears nowhere in the
  corpus and is still being honoured — it lives in the personal preference file, which never
  becomes a pack rule.
- **No prose.** The one keeper was expressible as a check, so the `RULES.md` ration went unspent and
  the upgrade pass over this run's own additions had nothing to convert.

### Verification, and why CI is red

Locally: `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` clean, with the advisory set byte-identical to
the pre-change run; suite 3725/3729, the four failures pre-existing (two shallow-clone guards that
fail loudly by design in this checkout, and the two `local-rules` rehearsals — both reproduced with
this change stashed).

CI run 35334042712 is red with `# fail 3`, and **none of the three is this diff**. Both are defects
on `main` that every PR now inherits, filed rather than folded in here — this PR's automerge policy
is `under:.claudinite/local`, and widening it to carry either fix is exactly the speed bump the
policy exists to be:

- `not ok 1013` — `SURFACE.GENERATED.md` is stale since #2101 left `github-pages` out of two rows
  (#2125).
- `not ok 3650` — the `local-rules` rehearsal's two modes, red since #2058 pointed the fixture's
  `$schema` at a pack its member never declares (#2128).

Auto-merge could not be armed against that red, so this PR is left open with its reason stated.

Refs #2119
